A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QEP research. All 16 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including appendices, tables, figures, and equations, are readable and support comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama-2 quantization experiments, including perplexity, zero-shot accuracy, runtime, error propagation, and calibration-distribution robustness results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds QuIP comparisons, Llama-3 and Mistral results, and a five-seed QuIP stability study.

M1.justification: The decoupled-activation objective, closed-form weight correction, tunable propagation strength, and Hessian damping remain unchanged. Damping moves from Section 5.4 to Appendix B.1. The new ridge-regularization discussion provides theoretical interpretation rather than a changed quantization procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use C4/Pile calibration, WikiText2/PTB/C4 perplexity evaluation, and ARC-Easy/PIQA/StoryCloze zero-shot evaluation. The calibration-distribution scenarios are also retained. Additional model families expand model configurations rather than datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated QuIP, with and without QEP, to the per-channel INT4/INT3/INT2 comparisons in Tables 1 and 2; v1 evaluated RTN, GPTQ, and AWQ. QuIP was previously only discussed. FP16 reference comparisons disappear, while the grouped-quantization comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama-3-8B and Mistral-7B configurations across three precisions. The error-growth experiment's stated intervention also changes: v1 Figure 1 corrects later full-precision blocks, whereas v2 Figure 2 describes QEP-enhanced quantization of the first ten blocks. This is a reported protocol revision; the PDFs do not establish whether that experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 and Figure 3 add a focused analysis of whether QuIP's gains with QEP persist across random seeds. The existing calibration-distribution robustness results in Table 4 remain unchanged. The error-growth analysis is retained with a revised intervention description.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates. v2 introduces five independent runs per QuIP configuration, means, and standard-error bars in Figure 3, and discloses best-seed reporting for the main QuIP comparisons. This establishes a new uncertainty-reporting practice, limited to QuIP.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial QuIP, Llama-3, Mistral, and seed-averaged results. For example, its new INT2 QuIP comparison on Llama-2-7B reports WikiText2 perplexities of 65.593 without QEP and 11.972 with QEP. The 864 matched quantized Llama-2 entries across six datasets/tasks remain unchanged apart from equivalent rounding. FP16 results and grouped average-accuracy rows are removed.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's closed-form correction proof, v2 adds first-order error-propagation analyses, exponential-growth bounds, a claimed QEP error-dominance guarantee, propagation-strength monotonicity, ridge-regularization relationships, and supporting lemmas in Appendix A. These are substantial theoretical additions, although their proofs contain consequential errors.

C1.justification: The central claims about accumulated quantization errors, QEP correction, low-bit benefits, and compatibility remain. v2's conclusion adds explicit positioning alongside nonlinear and block-wise quantization and the prospective claim that combining these approaches could exceed QAT performance, without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: The existing error-accumulation and calibration-overfitting explanations remain. v2 adds a claimed ridge-regularization interpretation of propagation strength and interprets the seed study as evidence that QuIP gains are reproducible. It also clarifies that QEP+RTN runtime largely measures correction preprocessing.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies alpha=1/2, except alpha=0 for Llama-2-70B MLP layers, and identifies QuIP's C4 calibration. These are disclosures rather than established changes to retained experiments. Hardware, calibration sample budget, and damping remain unchanged. Conversely, Table 4 loses v1's explicit INT3g128 setting.

R1.justification: Section 2 is substantively reorganized around compensation-, rotation-, and salience-based PTQ, with stronger positioning against block-wise and global fine-tuning approaches. References such as LeanQuant, additive quantization, and Optimal Brain Compression are added, while discussions and citations of CBQ, LRQuant, AffineQuant, and several general quantization works are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, background, method explanations, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Experimental subsections are consolidated, equation numbering is revised, damping moves into an implementation appendix, and the appendices are reorganized into theory, implementation, and experiments. This substantially changes the presentation of retained material.

P2.justification: v2 adds a results-summary bar chart and a seed-uncertainty figure, redraws the error-growth figure, and rebuilds the result tables with model columns, vertically stacked precision groups, and shaded QEP rows. Grouped perplexity results move into Appendix C, and runtime/robustness tables become embedded beside the discussion.

improvement.justification: Broader model and QuIP comparisons, five-seed uncertainty reporting, and explicit alpha defaults improve empirical support and reproducibility. However, the new theoretical guarantees contain serious proof defects: Theorem A.4 reverses a matrix-norm inequality, and Proposition A.3 treats an upper bound on the input norm as a lower bound. These problems undermine the added theoretical claims and counteract the empirical and documentation benefits, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
